raw_segments.text: As I was going upstairs to fetch my portfolio and pencils, Mrs. Fairfax called to me.
"'Your morning school hours are over now, I suppose,' said she.
She was in a room the folding doors of which stood open.
I went in when she addressed me.
It was a large, stately apartment with purple chairs and curtains, a turkey carpet, walnut-paneled
walls, one vast window rich in stained glass, and a lofty ceiling, nobly molded.
Mrs. Fairfax was dusting some vases of fine purple spar, which stood on a sideboard.
